meaning_fixes.reason: Translator flagged uncertainty: source 'tsuranuku tte yakusoku shitanda!' pairs 'yakusoku' (promise/swore) with 'tsuranuku' (lit. 'pierce through', figuratively 'carry it through / see it to the end'); no named attack/technique matches 'tsuranuku' in the glossary, so it is Renton's resolve, not a move name. 'I made that promise!' dropped the 'carry it through' content entirely, leaving only a vague 'that promise' with no recoverable referent. Fixed to 'I swore to push on!' (19 chars, under the 20-char budget), which keeps both the vow and the 'see it through' sense.

checked_decisions.finding: 'Matte-cha dame da, kyousuccha dame da!' ('can't wait, can't beg!') echoes the Eureka Seven motto's 'don't beg' theme; translated as 'Can't wait, can't beg!', an accurate parallel-structure rendering, consistent with terms_028.json's note on the motto without needing its exact (much longer) official wording.

'Ikite kaeru tte yakusoku shite kudasai!' ('please promise you'll come back alive!') is Renton (sole pilot of this resource) addressing this request outward, e.g. to Eureka or an ally, not a request made of himself; translation 'Promise you'll return alive!' correctly keeps the outward address.

Translator flagged 'dokkara datte koi!' (lit. 'come from anywhere!') rendered as the idiom 'Bring it on!' to fit an 18-char budget. Ruling: acceptable -- preserves the defiant challenge without reversing meaning.
Locked unit name 'theEND' (lowercase 'the' + uppercase 'END') is preserved correctly in every occurrence in the Anemone portion of this slice, matching unit_names_014_b.json ('Nirvash theEND').
